title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses

object.carrier: Seven persistent-carrier families in agent harnesses: memory (F1), reusable skills (F2), Tool/MCP state (F3), memory-to-skill transformation (T2), subagent delegation (T3-S), session summary (T3-C), shared artifact (T3-A)

safety_property.statement: Whether attacker-influenced content persisted in a harness carrier can cross a declared boundary (session, process, agent-instance, or workspace) and, when re-consumed by an independently benign later trigger, produce an oracle-verified confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authorization violation; safety failure is declared only on executed-effect evidence (N5a/N5b), and containment is judged by the furthest evidence-supported lifecycle stage rather than a binary outcome.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Five-element Persistent-Risk Lifecycle K=<E,C,B,T,V>; each run assigned the furthest trace-evidence-supported stage N0-N5b; ASR = share of eligible scored runs reaching N5a/N5b; CSS = stage-weighted score (100 at N0 down to 0 at N5b, higher = earlier containment); five-arm matched controls (clean-source, no-persist, no-trigger, cleanup) attribute violations to lifecycle elements.

capabilities: Controls low-trust content that reaches the harness (tool/MCP outputs, schemas, metadata, workspace notes, skill packages, memory writes) and is retained in persistent carriers
Planting occurs before a declared session/process/agent/workspace boundary; payload need not survive verbatim through summarization, synthesis, delegation, or transfer
Cannot alter the later benign trigger or the harness/model internals
assumptions: The trigger T is independently benign: it neither contains the adversarial instruction nor requests or authorizes the oracle-defined violating action
Every configuration runs under the most permissive natively supported non-interactive approval profile
One scored attack attempt per case and configuration; replacement attempts only for execution-invalid runs
Violations require case-specific hard oracles (executed effect, committed file operation, or honeypot canary), never model self-reports or suspicious text
not_covered: Adaptive attackers reacting to deployed defenses
Real-world harm magnitude and severity (CSS measures lifecycle progression only)
Same-stage prompt injection (excluded by the independently-benign-trigger requirement)
Product-default permission profiles (evaluation uses the most permissive mode)

intervention.name: HarnessSafe benchmark (evaluation instrument; no deployed defense)
intervention.description: The paper contributes a 328-case cross-harness benchmark specified as five-element Persistent-Risk Lifecycles with harness-native bindings across seven harnesses, plus a multi-stage trace-based evaluation (N0-N5b) with CSS/ASR metrics that localizes where each attack chain is contained. The matched-control arms (clean-source, no-persist, no-trigger, cleanup) manipulate lifecycle elements as experimental controls for attribution, not as proposed defenses.

controls.name: Clean-source arm (entry E replaced with interface-matched benign source)
No-persist arm (declared carrier blocked/removed before boundary)
No-trigger arm (activating prompt replaced with neutral benign task)
Cleanup arm (persisted carrier removed immediately before trigger)
Family-wise common-support sets (e.g., 281-case six-backend intersection, 279-case five-arm intersection)

results.claim: HarnessSafe is a benchmark of 328 executable persistent-risk cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families, evaluated natively on mainstream agent harnesses.
results.setting: Seven persistent-carrier families (F1-F3, T2, T3-S/C/A); seven harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent)
results.quote: To this end, we present HarnessSafe, a benchmark comprising 328 executable cases across seven persistent-carrier families and evaluated on most mainstream agent harnesses.

results.claim: Holding the backend GPT-5.6-Sol fixed, changing only the harness moves standardized CSS from 39.4 (Claude Code) to 62.3 (Codex CLI), so containment is shaped by the harness, not the model label alone.
results.comparison: 39.4 (Claude Code) -> 62.3 (Codex CLI) with GPT-5.6-Sol fixed; backend-only range 22.7 to 58.7 within Claude Code
results.setting: 328-case benchmark, most permissive non-interactive profiles, seven harness-model configurations (Exp1/Exp2)
results.quote: With GPT-5.6-Sol fixed, changing the harness moves CSS from 39.4 under Claude Code to 62.3 under Codex CLI; with Claude Code fixed, changing the backend produces a CSS range from 22.7 to 58.7.

results.claim: Within the fixed Claude Code harness, varying only the model backend moves overall CSS from 58.7 (Claude Sonnet 4.6) down to 22.7 (MiniMax M2.5), showing containment is a property of the full configuration.
results.setting: Claude Code 2.1.133 fixed (skip-permissions, isolated home, tool surface, 328 cases); six backends varied (Exp2)
results.quote: In Table 2, Overall CSS spans 22.7 for MiniMax M2.5 to 58.7 for Claude Sonnet 4.6.

results.claim: Containment is family-specific: within Exp1, the best overall configuration (Codex CLI) leads five of the seven family columns—60.0 on F1 Memory, 64.3 on F3 Tool/MCP, 88.2 on T2 Memory-to-Skill, 84.3 on T3-C Session Summary, and 93.3 on T3-A Shared Artifact—but records the lowest reusable-skill (F2) CSS of 47.0, where Claude Code leads at 70.0, and on the remaining family T3-S Subagent Delegation, OpenCode leads at 64.0, whereas Codex scores 46.7.
results.comparison: Codex leads five of seven families (60.0 F1, 64.3 F3, 88.2 T2, 84.3 T3-C, 93.3 T3-A) but is lowest on F2 Skill at 47.0
results.setting: Exp1 cross-harness comparison on family-specific common support, 328-case benchmark
results.quote: Codex leads five of the seven family columns—60.0 on F1 Memory, 64.3 on F3 Tool/MCP, 88.2 on T2 Memory-to-Skill, 84.3 on T3-C Session Summary, and 93.3 on T3-A Shared Artifact—but records the lowest F2 Skill score, 47.0, where Claude Code leads at 70.0.

results.claim: Configurations with nearly identical ASR (OpenCode 10.08% vs Hermes Agent 10.81%) stop at different lifecycle stages (mostly N1 vs N2/N4), so endpoint ASR conceals distinct residual risks.
results.setting: Exp1: OpenCode/Qwen 3.7 Plus vs Hermes Agent/Kimi K3 on the 328-case benchmark
results.quote: Figure 3 shows that similar ASRs can mask distinct stopping profiles: OpenCode and Hermes (10.08% vs. 10.81%) stop more often at N1, N2 and N4, respectively.

denominator.n_valid: OpenCode 258 and Hermes Agent 296 evaluation-eligible scored rows
denominator.how_counted: Appendix F.1 Table 15: A/S per configuration - OpenCode 26/258, Hermes Agent 32/296

results.claim: Matched controls show the observed violations depend on the full attack lifecycle: relative to the full-attack ASR of 25.8%, removing any single lifecycle element drops ASR to 0.4% (clean-source), 2.5% (no-persist), 0.0% (no-trigger), or 1.8% (cleanup).
results.setting: Claude Code 2.1.133 with Claude Haiku 4.5, maximum-permission non-interactive profile, isolated-home execution, 279 strictly paired five-arm cases
results.quote: Relative to the full-attack ASR of 25.8%, ASR is 0.4% in the clean-source arm, 2.5% in the no-persist arm, 0.0% in the no-trigger arm, and 1.8% in the cleanup arm.

denominator.n_valid: 279 strictly paired cases eligible in every arm (five-arm intersection)
denominator.how_counted: Appendix G.4 Table 20: pooled N5a+N5b counts 72/279 (full), 1/279 (clean-source), 7/279 (no-persist), 0/279 (no-trigger), 5/279 (cleanup)

results.claim: Under the best-containing configuration (Codex CLI with GPT-5.6-Sol), oracle-verified attack success is 3.96% (13 of 328 eligible rows) at full coverage.
results.setting: Codex CLI 0.145.0 with GPT-5.6-Sol, danger-full-access non-interactive profile, 328-case benchmark
results.quote: Codex CLI's native evaluation pipeline yields 328 eligible rows, 13 N5a+N5b outcomes (8 N5a and 5 N5b), and an ASR of 13/328=3.96%

denominator.how_counted: 13 N5a+N5b outcomes over 328 eligible rows (Appendix F.1, Table 15)

results.claim: In the fixed Claude Code harness, the Claude Haiku 4.5 configuration that the paper selects for Exp3 as the one with the widest dynamic range for a removal effect reaches a 24.70% (81/328) oracle-verified full-benchmark ASR, a different estimand from the matched-control full-attack arm's 72/279=25.8% on the 279-case shared support.
results.setting: Claude Code 2.1.133 with Claude Haiku 4.5, skip-permissions profile, full 328-case benchmark (Exp2)
results.quote: The full-benchmark Haiku attack result on 328 cases, 81/328=24.70%

denominator.n_valid: 328 evaluation-eligible scored rows for Claude Haiku 4.5
denominator.how_counted: 81 N5a+N5b outcomes over 328 eligible rows (Appendix F.3, Tables 16-17)

limitations.statement: Scores characterize performance on the final benchmark inventory, not the prevalence of these mechanisms in a real-world population.
limitations.quote: The resulting scores therefore characterize performance on the final HarnessSafe benchmark rather than the prevalence of these mechanisms in a real-world population.

limitations.statement: CSS measures how far an attack chain progresses, not real-world harm magnitude or severity.
limitations.quote: CSS measures attack progression rather than harm magnitude; impact type and severity remain separate attributes.

limitations.statement: Reduced-support results (fewer than 328 cases due to missing native harness support) are not directly comparable to full-support results.
limitations.quote: An asterisk (*) marks a result evaluated on fewer than 328 cases because the configuration lacks native support for some cases; such results are not directly comparable to full-support results.

limitations.statement: The artifact does not allow independent reconstruction of the within-case five-arm pairing for the matched-control experiment.
limitations.quote: the submission package does not support independent reconstruction of the complete within-case five-arm pairing.

limitations.statement: Native execution evidence is only representative, not exhaustive, for nine of the twelve evaluated configurations.
limitations.quote: For the remaining nine local configurations, the package provides representative rather than exhaustive native execution evidence.

limitations.statement: Sampling parameters, decoding tuples, and stage timeouts were not retained for several configurations, so cross-harness measurements characterize whole evaluated configurations rather than an isolated model or harness.
limitations.quote: "Not retained" means that the supplied paper artifacts do not consolidate one value for the corresponding configuration; no value is inferred retroactively.
